nodes.name: Electrodeposition of NiFe LDH on NF
nodes.procedure: Initially, the NF substrate was adopted to load NiFe LDH through an electrodeposited method. (Optimized conditions such as nickel-iron ratio, electrodeposition potential, and electrodeposition time were used.)
nodes.source_text: The S-NiFe LDH/NF was synthesized through electrochemical deposition and subsequent ion exchange strategy (Scheme 1). Initially, the NF substrate was adopted to load NiFe LDH through an electrodeposited method.

nodes.name: Ion Exchange Sulfur Doping
nodes.procedure: Then, the NiFe LDH/NF was submerged in a Na₂S solution at room temperature, which resulted in the creation of S-doped NiFe LDH/NF. This occurred through an ion exchange mechanism where OH⁻ ions were partially replaced by S²⁻ ions. Throughout this process, the color of the sample undergoes a transition from silver gray to yellow and ultimately to black-yellow.

nodes.description: OER performance in alkaline freshwater (1.0 M KOH)
nodes.source_text: The OER performance of the different electrocatalysts was investigated through a typical three-electrode system. All potentials were corrected using iR compensation and converted to reversible hydrogen electrodes (RHE)... the overpotential at 100 mA cm^{-2} for S-NiFe LDH is significantly reduced to only 224 mV... even at 500 and 1000 mA cm^{-2}, the activity of S-NiFe LDH (η_{500} = 261 mV, η_{1000} = 275 mV)... The calculated C_{dl} value for S-NiFe LDH (3.70 mF cm^{-2})... ECSA was evaluated to be 92.5 cm^2... S-NiFe LDH can maintain a consistent current density for 100 h at an overpotential of 0.224 V... sustain nearly constant potential for 200 h at both 100 and 500 mA cm^{-2}... Faraday efficiency close to 99%

nodes.description: OER performance in alkaline seawater (1.0 M KOH + seawater)
nodes.source_text: When the alkaline seawater is utilized as the electrolyte, the required overpotentials at these current densities are respectively recorded as 237, 283, and 299 mV... Tafel slope of S-NiFe LDH in alkaline seawater exhibits a marginal increase to 51.36 mV dec^{-1}... can operate stably at 500 mA cm^{-2} more than 200 h... E_corr and I_corr for S-NiFe LDH, respectively, are 0.396 V and 1.05 mA cm^{-2}... no hypochlorite species is detected

nodes.description: OER performance in alkaline simulated seawater

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of S-NiFe LDH/NF and NiFe LDH/NF show three Ni peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, 76.4° from NF substrate (JCPDS No. 04-0850); remaining peaks match NiFe LDH (JCPDS No. 40-0215) with no position shift but weakened intensities after S incorporation indicating decreased crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of three distinct peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76.4° in the XRD patterns of NiFe LDH/NF stem are from the NF substrate (JCPDS No. 04-0850) (Figure 1a). The remaining diffraction peaks are well-pointed to the diffraction peaks of NiFe LDH (JCPDS No. 40-0215). Upon S incorporation, the diffraction peak positions associated with NiFe LDH exhibit no variation, indicating the consistent crystalline structure, while the intensities of those are weakened, suggesting the decreased crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows preserved nanosheet array morphology after sulfurization on nickel foam substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After sulfurization, the morphology of NiFe LDH is well preserved (Figure 1b,c; Figure S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice fringes of 0.216 nm, 0.253 nm, and 0.378 nm corresponding to (015), (018), and (119) facets of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice stripes of 0.216, 0.253, and 0.378 nm observed in the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images correspond to the (015), (018), and (119) facets of NiFe LDH (Figure 1d,e), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX shows homogeneous dispersion of Ni, Fe, S, O with atomic ratio ≈1.03:1.05:0.32:7.60.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the energy dispersive x-ray (EDX) images reveal a homogeneous dispersion of its constituent elements with a relative atomic ratio of ≈1.03:1.05:0.32:7.60 for Ni, Fe, S, and O, respectively (Figure 1f; Figure S5, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows M-O at 508 cm⁻¹, M-OH at 682 cm⁻¹ (diminished after S-doping), Ni-S at ≈1020 cm⁻¹, SO₄²⁻ at 1114 cm⁻¹, NO₃⁻ at 1384 cm⁻¹, and H₂O at 3400 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at 508 and 682 cm⁻¹ respectively originate from the stretching patterns of M-O and M-OH. After sulfurization, the intensity of the peak assigned to M-OH is comparatively diminished... The weak peak emerged at ≈1020 cm⁻¹ indicates the formation of Ni-S bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni²⁺ at 856.0/873.7 eV, Ni-S/Ni⁰ at 852.7 eV, Fe 2p₃/₂ at 712.5 eV and 2p₁/₂ at 725.7 eV, S 2p at 163.3/162.1 eV (M-S) and 168.2 eV (SO₄²⁻), O 1s peaks at 529.5/531.4/532.9 eV; S-doping causes peak shifts indicating electronic structure changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Ni 2p spectra (Figure 2c), the two dominant peaks at 856.0 and 873.7 eV suggest the existence of Ni²⁺... the peak at 852.7 eV is the response of the Ni-S bond... The dominant peaks observed at 712.5 and 725.7 eV in the Fe 2p spectra are indicative of the Fe 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂ orbitals... The peaks appeared at 163.3 and 162.1 eV in the S 2p spectra indicating the presence of M-S bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mott-Schottky plots show positive slopes confirming n-type semiconductors for both; S-NiFe LDH slope = 8.33×10¹¹ (vs NiFe LDH 2.76×10¹²), carrier concentration = 4.71×10¹⁷ cm⁻³.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding mott-schottky (M-S) plots reveal that both electrocatalysts all have positive slopes (Figure 3a,b), suggesting their classification as n-type semiconductors, and the sulfurization does not change the semiconductor type of the electrocatalysts. The slope of NiFe LDH is 2.76×10¹², and after sulfurization, the slope of S-NiFe LDH decreases to 8.33×10¹¹, and the carrier concentration increases to 4.71×10¹⁷.

nodes.characterization_summary: Tauc plots give bandgap Eg = 2.23 eV for S-NiFe LDH (vs 2.35 eV for NiFe LDH).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated Eg value for S-NiFe LDH is 2.23 eV, which is smaller than that for NiFe LDH (2.35 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: S-NiFe LDH is superhydrophilic (immediate water adsorption); bubble CA = 163.1° vs 141.7° for NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For S-NiFe LDH, water droplets are immediately adsorbed upon addition to the electrocatalyst surface... indicating its superhydrophilic nature. Furthermore... S-NiFe LDH demonstrates a significantly larger CA of 163.1° compared to the CA of 141.7° observed for NiFe LDH.
